newsitem.title: UK: Courtaulds cuts UK viscose fibre capacity.
newsitem.headline: Courtaulds cuts UK viscose fibre capacity.

text.p: British chemical company Courtaulds Plc said on Wednesday it would cut its viscose fibre capacity in Europe due to poor trading conditions.
The company said it would reduce viscose capacity by 25,000 tonnes per annum at its plant in Grimsby, northern England.
The cuts at Grimsby would reduce the company's total European viscose capacity by 20 percent.
About 90 employees would be affected, although most would be redeployed at the Grimsby site, the firm said.
"Viscose is slowly recovering from its low point last summer, but capacity still exceeds demand, and trading remains unsatisfactory," Courtaulds chief executive Gordon Campbell said in a statement.
"There is no prospect within an acceptable time frame for material improvement to this situation," he added.
The company said it had improved trading in each of its businesses -- excluding viscose fibres -- despite the sluggishness of continental European economies.

"However, a combination of the strength of sterling, in terms both of its effect on trading and of translation, and the sale last year of four non-core businesses, limits the extent to which this improvement is reflected in profits," Campbell said.
